title: Iran Could Retrieve Uranium at Site U.S. Bombed Last Year, Officials Say
partialText: The fate of the highly enriched uranium and the options for securing it have become critical issues for the Trump administration.

title: How the War in Iran Is Disrupting the World’s Oil
partialText: Our business reporter Peter Eavis looks at the global implications of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway to the south of Iran. He analyzes ship activity in the strait, comparing it before and after the United States and Israel initiated attacks on Iran.

title: Israeli Strikes on Fuel Depots Send Black Clouds Over Iranian Capital
partialText: Immense dark plumes of smoke enveloped Tehran after the Israeli military expanded attacks on energy infrastructure.

title: Trump Executive Order Protected Weedkiller Roundup and a Munition, White Phosphorus
partialText: Citing national security, an unusual executive order gave protection to the herbicide Roundup. It also protected the U.S.’s only supply of a controversial, highly flammable munition.

title: Judge Voids Mass Layoffs at Voice of America
partialText: The ruling, which said that Kari Lake’s appointment to oversee V.O.A.’s parent agency was invalid, was a major rejection of President Trump’s attempts to dismantle the government-funded news group.

title: Trump Assembles a New Coalition to ‘Eradicate’ Cartels
partialText: At a gathering in Florida, the president asked the leaders of a dozen Latin American and Caribbean nations to help the U.S. military crush armed trafficking groups.

title: When DOGE Unleashed ChatGPT on the Humanities
partialText: Documents show how A.I. was used to cancel most previously approved grants by the National Endowment for the Humanities as the agency embraced President Trump’s agenda.

title: A Year After His Arrest, Mahmoud Khalil Lives in Limbo and in Fear
partialText: President Trump made Mr. Khalil the face of his crackdown on pro-Palestinian protests. Mr. Khalil is now living with uncertainty as the courts consider his deportation.

title: ICE Detention of Teen Musicians Roils Texas Mariachi Community
partialText: Two brothers who were recognized by their congresswoman last year, along with their parents and younger brother, are facing deportation.

title: The Met Opera’s Desperate Hunt for Money
partialText: The Met has looked to a foreign government, to new strategies, even to outer space, in its scramble to find money to sustain the country’s largest performing arts organization.

title: Trump Wants to ‘Take Over’ Elections. These States are Prime Targets.
partialText: President Trump thinks Republicans should control voting procedures in parts of the United States. But where? Here are some possibilities.

title: In Kentucky, Trump Allies Clash With Massie Over Iran War
partialText: Representative Thomas Massie’s race against a rival backed by President Trump is shaping up as a key midterm testing ground for G.O.P. attitudes on the war.

title: The Future We Feared Is Already Here
partialText: The showdown between the Pentagon and Anthropic is a window into how unprepared we are for the questions we are facing.

title: History Makers
partialText: On this International Women’s Day, we’re writing about a project to unearth stories of remarkable women.

title: Oscars 2026: Who Will Win, and Who Should Win?
partialText: Our critic on the remarkable movies and performances you don’t want to miss.

title: Oslo Police Investigate Explosion Outside U.S. Embassy
partialText: A motive for the explosion was unclear as of Sunday morning, but the police were investigating and said it appeared to be a “targeted attack.”

title: Smoking Jars of Metal and Fuses Thrown at Protest Near Mayor’s House
partialText: Six people were arrested after anti-Islamic protesters led by the right-wing activist Jake Lang clashed with counterprotesters near Gracie Mansion.

title: Ahead of Colombia’s Elections, Violence on the Campaign Trail Rattles Politicians
partialText: Politicians in Colombia have increasingly become targets of violence. A rise in kidnappings, death threats and assassinations has shaken the country ahead of the vote.

title: Gen Z-Backed Rapper Is on Course to Lead Nepal With Landslide Win
partialText: A youth-led uprising brought Nepal’s government down last year. Now, a 35-year-old politician demanding change is set to become prime minister.
